### StatusTag (`status-tag`)

State pill with a dot (running, queued, paused, failed, draft…). The state → tone mapping is a prop-driven dictionary merged over generic defaults, so products add their own states without touching the component.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `StatusTag` · group Display · status stable
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/StatusTag/StatusTag.doc.ts
- Registry dependencies: badge, ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add status-tag`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject status-tag`

Tokens: success, success-text, info, warning, warning-text, destructive, destructive-text, muted-foreground

Usage:

```tsx
import { StatusTag } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import type { StatusDefinition } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

/** Product-specific states are passed in, never hardcoded in the component. */
const DEPLOYMENT_STATES: Record<string, StatusDefinition> = {
  building: { label: 'Building', tone: 'info' },
  live: { label: 'Live', tone: 'primary' },
  rolled_back: { label: 'Rolled back', tone: 'warning' },
};

export default function StatusTagStates() {
  return (
    <div className="grid gap-3">
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2.5">
        {['running', 'queued', 'paused', 'draft', 'degraded', 'failed'].map((s) => (
          <StatusTag key={s} status={s} />
        ))}
      </div>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2.5">
        {['building', 'live', 'rolled_back'].map((s) => (
          <StatusTag key={s} status={s} statuses={DEPLOYMENT_STATES} uppercase size="sm" />
        ))}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Table (`table`)

Styled semantic table parts: Table, TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter, TableRow (selected state), TableHead (optional sort button with aria-sort), TableCell and TableCaption. Compact or comfortable density and an optional sticky header.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Table` · group Display · status stable
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Table/Table.doc.ts
- ARIA pattern: table (sortable columns)
- Registry dependencies: ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add table`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject table`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus between sortable column headers and interactive cells |
| Enter | On a sortable header: sorts ascending, then toggles ascending ⇄ descending (aria-sort) |
| Space | On a sortable header: same as Enter |

Tokens: border, card, secondary, accent, primary, foreground, muted-foreground, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { DEPLOYMENTS, count } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

const checkboxClass = 'size-4 cursor-interactive accent-primary focus-ring';

export default function TableSelectable() {
  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Set<number>>(new Set([2]));
  const toggle = (id: number) =>
    setSelected((prev) => {
      const next = new Set(prev);
      if (next.has(id)) next.delete(id);
      else next.add(id);
      return next;
    });
  return (
    <div className="overflow-hidden rounded-lg border border-border bg-card">
      <Table density="compact" stickyHeader containerClassName="max-h-64" containerLabel="Deployments">
        <TableCaption srOnly>Deployments, compact view with selection</TableCaption>
        <TableHeader>
          <TableRow>
            <TableHead className="w-10">
              <span className="sr-only">Select</span>
            </TableHead>
            <TableHead>Deployment</TableHead>
            <TableHead>Region</TableHead>
            <TableHead align="right">Requests</TableHead>
          </TableRow>
        </TableHeader>
        <TableBody>
          {DEPLOYMENTS.map((d) => (
            <TableRow key={d.id} selected={selected.has(d.id)}>
              <TableCell>
                <input
                  type="checkbox"
                  aria-label={`Select ${d.name}`}
                  checked={selected.has(d.id)}
                  onChange={() => toggle(d.id)}
                  className={checkboxClass}
                />
              </TableCell>
              <TableCell className="font-semibold">{d.name}</TableCell>
              <TableCell className="font-mono text-[12px] text-muted-foreground">{d.region}</TableCell>
              <TableCell align="right" className="font-mono text-[12.5px]">
                {count(d.requests)}
              </TableCell>
            </TableRow>
          ))}
        </TableBody>
      </Table>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Terminal (`terminal`)

Streamed command output (build, deploy, job logs). ANSI SGR colours map to contrast-safe tokens (`parseAnsi` is exported), `\r` progress lines rewrite in place, and a line cap drops the oldest output. It follows the tail until the user scrolls up, then offers “Jump to latest” with the count of new lines. Optional line numbers and timestamps, a wrap toggle, copy all and search with highlighted matches. The output is a `role="log"` with aria-live off unless `live` opts in. Stream through the `ref` handle (`write`, `writeln`, `clear`) or pass `lines`.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Terminal` · group Display · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Terminal/Terminal.doc.ts
- ARIA pattern: log · button · searchbox
- Registry dependencies: copy-button, live-announcer, ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add terminal`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject terminal`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves through the search box, match arrows, wrap toggle, copy button and the output log |
| End | In the log: jumps to the newest line and resumes following the tail |
| Home | In the log: jumps to the first line and stops following |
| Arrow keys / Page Up / Page Down | Scroll the focused log |
| Ctrl+F / ⌘F | Inside the terminal: focuses the search box |
| Enter / Shift+Enter | In the search box: next / previous match (scrolled into view) |
| Escape | In the search box: clears the search |

Tokens: card, background, border, popover, secondary, foreground, muted-foreground, destructive-text, success-text, warning-text, info, category-violet, warning, primary, primary-text, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { Play, RotateCcw } from '@gntik-ai/icons';
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { Button } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { Terminal, type TerminalHandle } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

const E = '\u001b[';
/** A fake build: ANSI-coloured lines, one progress line rewritten with `\r`, then a summary. */
const SCRIPT: string[] = [
  `${E}2m$ ${E}0mpnpm build\n`,
  `${E}36minfo${E}0m  resolving 412 packages\n`,
  `${E}36minfo${E}0m  compiling ${E}1m@acme/web${E}0m\n`,
  'progress  25%',
  '\rprogress  50%',
  '\rprogress  75%',
  '\rprogress 100%\n',
  `${E}33mwarn${E}0m  bundle "vendor" is 612 kB (limit 500 kB)\n`,
  `${E}32m✓${E}0m built in 4.2s · ${E}1m3 entries${E}0m\n`,
  `${E}31merror${E}0m  test "checkout › applies coupon" failed\n`,
  `${E}90m  at checkout.test.ts:42:7${E}0m\n`,
  `${E}1;31m✗ 1 failed${E}0m, ${E}32m128 passed${E}0m\n`,
];

export default function TerminalBuildLog() {
  const term = useRef<TerminalHandle>(null);
  const [running, setRunning] = useState(false);
  const [step, setStep] = useState(0);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!running) return;
    const id = window.setInterval(() => {
      setStep((n) => {
        const chunk = SCRIPT[n];
        if (chunk === undefined) {
          setRunning(false);
          return n;
        }
        term.current?.write(chunk);
        return n + 1;
      });
    }, 350);
    return () => window.clearInterval(id);
  }, [running]);

  return (
    <div className="grid w-full max-w-2xl gap-3">
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <Button size="sm" icon={Play} disabled={running || step >= SCRIPT.length} onClick={() => setRunning(true)}>
          Run build
        </Button>
        <Button
          size="sm"
          variant="secondary"
          icon={RotateCcw}
          onClick={() => {
            setRunning(false);
            setStep(0);
            term.current?.clear();
          }}
        >
          Reset
        </Button>
      </div>
      <Terminal
        ref={term}
        title="build · main"
        showLineNumbers
        emptyText="Press “Run build” to stream output."
        className="h-72"
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Text (`text`)

Named type roles for body copy, labels, captions and headings on the brand scale. Text uses text-body, text-label, text-supporting, text-caption and text-display; code stays relative at 0.92em within its parent. Heading sizes display, xl, lg, md, sm, xs and 2xs use text-display and text-heading-* independently of semantic level 1–6 (level 2 defaults to text-heading-lg). Eleven roles come from typography.css, also exported as DTCG typography, Figma type/* variables and typeScale with pixel dimensions and unitless leading. font-*, leading-* and tracking-* utilities override role defaults; body, supporting and caption inherit weight and tracking. A font-size className such as text-[32px] replaces the entire role, including its leading, weight and tracking: unlike the previous separate variant classes, those defaults no longer remain. Supply explicit utilities when needed, for example text-[32px] font-bold tracking-tight for display, text-[12px] font-medium leading-tight for label, or text-[16px] font-semibold tracking-tight leading-snug for Heading. Both components support contrast-safe tones, truncation, line clamping and as / render.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Text` · group Display · status stable
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Text/Text.doc.ts
- Primitive: `@base-ui/react/use-render`
- Registry dependencies: ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add text`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject text`

Tokens: type-display-size, type-heading-xl-size, type-heading-lg-size, type-heading-md-size, type-heading-sm-size, type-heading-xs-size, type-heading-2xs-size, type-body-size, type-label-size, type-supporting-size, type-caption-size, foreground, muted-foreground, primary-text, success-text, warning-text, destructive-text, secondary

Usage:

```tsx
import { Heading, Text } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

export default function TextRoles() {
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-[560px] gap-3">
      <Text variant="display">2.4k</Text>
      <Heading level={2}>Project overview</Heading>
      <Text>
        Deployments roll out region by region. Run <Text variant="code">deploy --canary</Text> to ship to a single
        region first.
      </Text>
      <Text variant="label">Billing email</Text>
      <Text variant="supporting">Invoices and receipts are sent to this address.</Text>
      <Text variant="caption">Updated 3 minutes ago</Text>
      <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-4">
        <Text variant="label" tone="primary">
          Active
        </Text>
        <Text variant="label" tone="success">
          Paid
        </Text>
        <Text variant="label" tone="warning">
          Due soon
        </Text>
        <Text variant="label" tone="destructive">
          Overdue
        </Text>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Thumbnail (`thumbnail`)

File or image preview tile: image or file-type icon with extension tag, name and size caption, upload progress (progressbar + shimmer that holds still under reduced motion), error state with retry, and a remove button. ThumbnailList lays tiles out as a wrapping list. Sizes use the shared formatBytes export (decimal SI by default); ThumbnailSizes demonstrates localized labels, IEC base, bits, display widths and precision. Built-in labels and sizes follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Thumbnail` · group Display · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Thumbnail/Thumbnail.doc.ts
- ARIA pattern: figure
- Registry dependencies: ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add thumbnail`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject thumbnail`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves to the remove button (and retry, in the error state) of each tile |
| Enter / Space | Activates remove or retry |

Tokens: card, border, secondary, muted-foreground, foreground, primary, destructive, destructive-text, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { I18nProvider } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { formatBytes, type FormatBytesOptions } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { Thumbnail, ThumbnailList } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

const FORMATS: FormatBytesOptions[] = [
  { locale: 'en' },
  { locale: 'es' },
  { unitDisplay: 'long' },
  { unitDisplay: 'narrow' },
  { base: 1024 },
  { base: 1024, locale: 'es', unitDisplay: 'long' },
  { unit: 'bit' },
  { unit: 'bit', unitDisplay: 'long' },
  { maximumFractionDigits: 2 },
];

/** Provider-localized sizes, a per-thumbnail override, and the shared formatter options. */
export default function ThumbnailSizes() {
  return (
    <div data-format-bytes-preview className="space-y-4">
      <I18nProvider locale="es">
        <ThumbnailList>
          <Thumbnail name="report-es.pdf" size={1536} />
          <Thumbnail name="report-en.pdf" size={1536} locale="en" />
        </ThumbnailList>
      </I18nProvider>
      <ul className="space-y-1 font-mono text-sm text-foreground">
        {FORMATS.map((options, index) => (
          <li key={index}>
            <code>{formatBytes(25_000_000, options)}</code>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Timestamp (`timestamp`)

A date in a <time dateTime> element: relative ("3 minutes ago", Intl.RelativeTimeFormat) or absolute (Intl.DateTimeFormat), localised with `locale`. Accepts a Date, ISO string or epoch ms. Relative labels refresh on an adaptive interval that is cleared on unmount. The full date shows in a tooltip on hover or focus and is also part of the accessible text. Display timeZone defaults to I18nProvider (system when unset); use the same zone on server and client. The TimeZone example shows the provider default and UTC overrides

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Timestamp` · group Display · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Timestamp/Timestamp.doc.ts
- Primitive: `@base-ui/react/tooltip`
- ARIA pattern: tooltip
- Registry dependencies: tooltip, ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add timestamp`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject timestamp`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Focuses the timestamp and shows the full date in a tooltip |
| Escape | Hides the tooltip |

Tokens: foreground, muted-foreground, border, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { TooltipProvider } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { Timestamp } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

const MINUTE = 60_000;

export default function TimestampActivity() {
  const [now] = useState(() => Date.now());
  const events = [
    { id: 1, text: 'Maria Ruiz deployed api-gateway to production', at: now - 3 * MINUTE },
    { id: 2, text: 'Invoice INV-2041 was paid', at: now - 2 * 60 * MINUTE },
    {
      id: 3,
      text: 'Daniel Okafor joined the Platform project',
      at: new Date(now - 3 * 24 * 60 * MINUTE).toISOString(),
    },
  ];
  return (
    <TooltipProvider>
      <ul className="w-full max-w-md divide-y divide-border rounded-md border border-border bg-card">
        {events.map((e) => (
          <li key={e.id} className="flex items-baseline justify-between gap-4 px-4 py-2.5 text-[13px] text-foreground">
            <span>{e.text}</span>
            <Timestamp value={e.at} className="shrink-0 text-[12px]" />
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </TooltipProvider>
  );
}
```

### Token (`token`)

Removable chip for active filters and recipient inputs: label with an optional muted prefix ("Region:"), a leading icon or avatar slot, tones (neutral, primary, success, warning, destructive), sizes sm and md, and an accessible "Remove {label}" button. Disabled tokens keep their label but cannot be removed.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Token` · group Display · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Token/Token.doc.ts
- ARIA pattern: button (remove)
- Registry dependencies: ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add token`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject token`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the remove button |
| Enter | Removes the token |
| Space | Removes the token |
| Backspace | Removes the token while its remove button is focused (also Delete) |

Tokens: tone, tone-text, tone-chip-text, border, background, foreground, muted-foreground, secondary, primary, primary-text, success-text, warning-text, destructive-text, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Token } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

const INITIAL = [
  { key: 'Status', value: 'Failed' },
  { key: 'Region', value: 'eu-west-1' },
  { key: 'Region', value: 'us-east-1' },
  { key: 'Owner', value: 'Platform team' },
];

export default function TokenFilters() {
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState(INITIAL);
  const remove = (index: number) => setFilters((list) => list.filter((_, i) => i !== index));
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
      <span className="font-mono text-[10px] tracking-[0.14em] text-muted-foreground uppercase">Filters</span>
      {filters.map((f, i) => (
        <Token key={`${f.key}-${f.value}`} prefix={`${f.key}:`} label={f.value} onRemove={() => remove(i)} />
      ))}
      {filters.length > 0 ? (
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => setFilters([])}
          className="inline-flex h-7 items-center rounded-md px-2 text-[12px] font-medium text-muted-foreground transition-colors hover:text-destructive-text focus-ring"
        >
          Clear all
        </button>
      ) : (
        <span className="text-[12px] text-muted-foreground">No filters applied</span>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### ToolCallCard (`tool-call-card`)

A tool invocation in an assistant turn: name, status (awaiting-approval, running, succeeded, failed, denied), duration and collapsible arguments, result or error. Failed and denied calls open by default. Entering awaiting-approval opens arguments unless open is controlled, announces the request politely once per entry and keeps focus where it was. The approval group remains visible even when collapsed. onApprove() and onDeny(reason?) report a decision; the caller must update status and decision (ToolCallDecision: outcome approved or denied, optional reason). Promise callbacks show loading and keep the disabled actions focusable until settled; rejection enables retry and the caller reports errors. askDenyReason defaults to true: Deny asks for a trimmed optional reason (empty becomes undefined); false denies immediately. destructive uses Run {name}, destructive tone and a reversibility hint. approveLabel and denyLabel override text; approvalPrompt accepts a ReactNode naming the group. The live example includes normal, destructive and controlled-closed approval, custom labels and prompt, immediate denial and recorded decisions. Approval must be enforced server-side: the backend must refuse unapproved calls; this card is not a security boundary.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/chat` · export `ToolCallCard` · group Display · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/chat/src/ToolCallCard/ToolCallCard.doc.ts
- Primitive: `@base-ui/react/collapsible`
- ARIA pattern: disclosure
- Install: `gntik-ui add tool-call-card`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject tool-call-card`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Enter | Expands or collapses the card (or a JSON section) |
| Space | Expands or collapses the card (or a JSON section) |
| Tab | Moves to JSON sections, scrollable code and approval controls; busy actions remain focusable |
| Enter / Space on Approve | Calls onApprove once; pending callbacks disable further decisions |
| Enter / Space on Deny | Focuses Reason (optional), or calls onDeny immediately with askDenyReason=false |
| Enter in Reason (optional) | Calls onDeny once with the trimmed reason or undefined; ignores IME composition |
| Escape in the reason step / Cancel | Cancels locally and focuses Deny without reporting a decision |

Tokens: card, border, secondary, muted-foreground, success-text, destructive, destructive-text, focus-ring, warning, warning-chip-text

Usage:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { useChatI18n } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { ToolCallCard, type ToolCallDecision, type ToolCallStatus } from '@gntik-ai/chat';

function ApprovalExample({ destructive = false, immediate = false }: { destructive?: boolean; immediate?: boolean }) {
  const { t, tc } = useChatI18n();
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<ToolCallStatus>('awaiting-approval');
  const [decision, setDecision] = useState<ToolCallDecision>();
  const name = destructive ? 'delete_project' : 'read_project';
  return (
    <ToolCallCard
      name={name}
      status={status}
      args={{ id: 'p1' }}
      destructive={destructive}
      askDenyReason={!immediate}
      approveLabel={immediate ? t('common.yes') : undefined}
      denyLabel={immediate ? t('common.no') : undefined}
      approvalPrompt={immediate ? <strong>{tc('toolCall.approvalPrompt')}</strong> : undefined}
      open={immediate ? false : undefined}
      decision={decision}
      result={status === 'succeeded' ? { ok: true } : undefined}
      onApprove={async () => {
        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800));
        setDecision({ outcome: 'approved' });
        setStatus('succeeded');
      }}
      onDeny={async (reason) => {
        await new Promise<void>((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800));
        setDecision({ outcome: 'denied', reason });
        setStatus('denied');
      }}
    />
  );
}

export default function ToolCallCardStates() {
  const { tc } = useChatI18n();
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-2xl flex-col gap-3">
      <ToolCallCard name="list_deployments" status="running" args={{ project: 'web-app', since: '2026-10-01' }} />
      <ToolCallCard
        name="search_invoices"
        status="succeeded"
        durationMs={840}
        defaultOpen
        args={{ month: '2026-09', status: 'unpaid' }}
        result={{ count: 2, total: { amount: 1840, currency: 'EUR' }, ids: ['INV-1042', 'INV-1047'] }}
      />
      <ToolCallCard
        name="invite_member"
        status="failed"
        durationMs={2310}
        args={{ email: 'alex@example.com', role: 'admin' }}
        error="Seat limit reached: the plan allows 20 members."
      />
      <ApprovalExample />
      <ApprovalExample destructive />
      <ApprovalExample immediate />
      <ToolCallCard
        name="delete_project"
        status="denied"
        args={{ id: 'p1' }}
        decision={{ outcome: 'denied', reason: tc('toolCall.exampleDenyReason') }}
      />
      <ToolCallCard
        name="read_project"
        status="succeeded"
        defaultOpen
        decision={{ outcome: 'approved' }}
        result={{ id: 'p1' }}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### VirtualList (`virtual-list`)

Windowed list for thousands of rows: only the visible rows plus `overscan` are mounted, with a fixed `itemHeight` or measured rows from an estimate. One roving tab stop, aria-setsize/posinset on every row, `scrollToIndex` through a ref, and a single-select `listbox` mode. No dependencies. Built-in labels follow I18nProvider (en/es); caller overrides take precedence. See the TransferList catalog defaults example for a live Spanish preview of this component.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `VirtualList` · group Display · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/VirtualList/VirtualList.doc.ts
- ARIA pattern: list / listbox with roving tabindex
- Registry dependencies: ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add virtual-list`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject virtual-list`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves focus to the active row (one tab stop) |
| ArrowDown / ArrowUp | Moves to the next / previous row, scrolling it into view |
| PageDown / PageUp | Moves one viewport down / up |
| Home / End | Moves to the first / last row |
| Enter | Activates the row (selects it in listbox mode) |
| Space | Listbox mode: selects the focused option |

Tokens: card, border, secondary, primary, foreground, muted-foreground, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';
import { Button } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { VirtualList, type VirtualListHandle } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

const levels = ['info', 'info', 'info', 'warn', 'info', 'error'] as const;
const logs = Array.from({ length: 5000 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: `log-${i}`,
  time: `12:${String(Math.floor(i / 60) % 60).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(i % 60).padStart(2, '0')}`,
  level: levels[i % levels.length] ?? 'info',
  message: `deploy-gate: checked deployment #${4100 + i} for open incidents`,
}));

const levelClass = {
  info: 'text-muted-foreground',
  warn: 'text-warning-text',
  error: 'text-destructive-text',
} as const;

export default function VirtualListLogs() {
  const list = useRef<VirtualListHandle>(null);
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-2xl flex-col gap-2">
      <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
        <h3 id="logs-title" className="flex-1 text-[13px] font-semibold text-foreground">
          Deployment log{' '}
          <span className="font-normal text-muted-foreground">· {logs.length.toLocaleString('en-US')} lines</span>
        </h3>
        <Button
          size="sm"
          variant="secondary"
          onClick={() => list.current?.scrollToIndex(logs.length - 1, { focus: true })}
        >
          Jump to latest
        </Button>
      </div>
      <VirtualList
        ref={list}
        aria-labelledby="logs-title"
        items={logs}
        getKey={(l) => l.id}
        itemHeight={30}
        height={280}
        rowClassName="gap-3 px-3 font-mono text-[12px]"
        renderItem={(l) => (
          <>
            <span className="shrink-0 text-muted-foreground tabular-nums">{l.time}</span>
            <span className={`w-10 shrink-0 font-semibold uppercase ${levelClass[l.level]}`}>{l.level}</span>
            <span className="min-w-0 truncate text-foreground">{l.message}</span>
          </>
        )}
      />
    </div>
  );
}
```

      actions={

          <Button size="sm" variant="ghost">

        </>
      }

    />
  );
}

### readSSE (`read-sse`)

Reads a streamed fetch response as an async iterator, for chat replies and live log tails where EventSource cannot be used (POST bodies, auth headers). `readSSE(response, { signal, maxBufferSize })` follows the WHATWG event-stream rules: streaming UTF-8, BOM, CRLF/LF/CR endings across chunk boundaries, comments, multi-line data, a persistent id and a digits-only retry. `readTextParts` splits on a separator (a line feed by default) for NDJSON. Aborting the signal, leaving the loop early or a stream error cancels the reader once, so the connection closes. An unterminated final block is dropped, as EventSource does. There is no reconnection: keep the last id and retry and send Last-Event-ID yourself. maxBufferSize bounds memory, not time, so abort a stream that goes quiet.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/chat` · export `readSSE` · group Feedback · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/chat/src/readSSE/readSSE.doc.ts
- Install: `gntik-ui add read-sse`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject read-sse`

Usage:

```tsx
import { Button } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { readSSE } from '@gntik-ai/chat';

// Stands in for fetch(url) so the example runs without a backend; in an app, pass the real response.
const encoder = new TextEncoder();

/**
 * Stands in for `fetch(url)` in the docs, so the examples need no backend: a streamed Response that
 * sends one chunk every `delayMs`, then closes, or fails with a network error when `failAfter` is set.
 */
function fakeStreamResponse(
  chunks: string[],
  { delayMs = 200, failAfter }: { delayMs?: number; failAfter?: number } = {},
) {
  let index = 0;
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;
  const stream = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    pull(controller) {
      return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
        timer = setTimeout(() => {
          if (index === failAfter) controller.error(new TypeError('network error'));
          else if (index < chunks.length) controller.enqueue(encoder.encode(chunks[index++]));
          else controller.close();
          resolve();
        }, delayMs);
      });
    },
    cancel() {
      clearTimeout(timer);
    },
  });
  return new Response(stream, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' } });
}

// What an OpenAI-style endpoint sends: JSON deltas, then a plain [DONE] the caller stops on.
const REPLY = ['The ', 'deployment ', 'finished ', 'without ', 'errors.'].map(
  (delta) => `data: ${JSON.stringify({ delta })}\n\n`,
);
const BODY = [': keep-alive\n\n', ...REPLY, 'data: [DONE]\n\n'];

const STATUS = {
  idle: 'Ready.',
  streaming: 'Streaming…',
  done: 'Done.',
  stopped: 'Stopped.',
  error: 'The stream failed.',
} as const;

/** Reads a chat reply token by token, with a Stop button wired to the same AbortController. */
export default function ReadSSEChatStream() {
  const [text, setText] = useState('');
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<keyof typeof STATUS>('idle');
  const controllerRef = useRef<AbortController | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => () => controllerRef.current?.abort(), []);

  async function send() {
    const controller = new AbortController();
    controllerRef.current = controller;
    setText('');
    setStatus('streaming');
    try {
      // In an app: const response = await fetch('/api/chat', { method: 'POST', body, signal: controller.signal });
      const response = fakeStreamResponse(BODY);
      for await (const message of readSSE(response, { signal: controller.signal })) {
        if (message.data === '[DONE]') break;
        const { delta } = JSON.parse(message.data) as { delta: string };
        setText((current) => current + delta);
      }
      setStatus('done');
    } catch {
      setStatus(controller.signal.aborted ? 'stopped' : 'error');
    }
  }

  const streaming = status === 'streaming';
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-xl flex-col gap-3">
      <div className="flex gap-2">
        <Button onClick={send} disabled={streaming}>
          Send
        </Button>
        <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => controllerRef.current?.abort()} disabled={!streaming}>
          Stop
        </Button>
      </div>
      <p className="min-h-6 text-foreground" aria-busy={streaming}>
        {text}
      </p>
      <p role="status" className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">
        {STATUS[status]}
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Toast (`toast`)

Short-lived notification stacked bottom-right. Five tones (neutral, success, info, warning, destructive) plus loading, title, description, a primary action and a dismiss action next to the close button; auto-dismiss pauses while the stack is hovered or focused. `toast.promise(task, { loading, success, error })` updates one toast in place (errors are announced assertively). Mount ToastProvider + Toaster once and queue with the useToast() hook.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Toast` · group Feedback · status stable
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Toast/Toast.doc.ts
- Primitive: `@base-ui/react/toast`
- ARIA pattern: region + live announcements (status)
- Registry dependencies: spinner, ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add toast`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject toast`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| F6 | Moves focus into the notifications region (pauses auto-dismiss) |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Reaches each toast’s primary action, dismiss action and close button |
| Enter / Space | On the close button or dismiss action: dismisses the toast (an action also runs its handler) |

Tokens: popover, popover-foreground, border, foreground, muted-foreground, success-text, info, warning-text, destructive-text, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { Button } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { ToastProvider, Toaster, useToast } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

function InviteButton() {
  const toast = useToast();
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('No reply yet');
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-col items-center gap-3">
      <Button
        variant="secondary"
        onClick={() =>
          toast.add({
            tone: 'info',
            title: 'You were invited to “Platform”',
            description: 'Join the workspace to see its projects.',
            timeout: 10000,
            action: { label: 'Accept', onClick: () => setStatus('Accepted') },
            dismissAction: { label: 'Not now', onClick: () => setStatus('Postponed') },
          })
        }
      >
        Show invitation
      </Button>
      <p className="h-4 text-[12px] text-muted-foreground">{status}</p>
    </div>
  );
}

export default function ToastActions() {
  return (
    <ToastProvider>
      <InviteButton />
      <Toaster />
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}
```

### useChat (`use-chat`)

Experimental streaming conversation runtime: useChat({ adapter, id, initialMessages, initialCursor, flushIntervalMs, generateId, onFinish, onError }) returns messages, isStreaming, error, sendMessage(text, attachments?), stop(), regenerate(messageId?), setMessages(next), loadOlder(), hasOlder and isLoadingOlder. Busy sends are ignored. Messages hold text, reasoning, tool, source, file and step parts. applyChunk is a pure UI-message-stream v1 reducer; unknown chunk types are ignored. Stop and unmount abort the adapter signal and retain partial parts; failed replies call onError once. State updates batch every 50 ms (0 commits every chunk). A changed conversation id aborts and resets. createEchoAdapter runs locally; createHttpChatAdapter reads UI-stream SSE and createOpenAICompatibleAdapter maps text-only chat-completions SSE. Both reuse readSSE and check HTTP status first. Their URL must be the product backend: provider keys stay server-side. Map pending/streaming to ChatMessage.streaming, and terminal replies to onRetry; ChatMessage has no status prop. See the chat runtime guide on this page for the protocol, history, abort and part mapping.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/chat` · export `useChat` · group Feedback · status experimental
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/chat/src/useChat/useChat.doc.ts
- Registry dependencies: attachment, citation, read-sse, tool-call-card
- Install: `gntik-ui add use-chat`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject use-chat`

Usage:

```tsx
import { ChatComposer } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { ChatAnnouncer, ChatMessage } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { Markdown } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { createEchoAdapter, useChat } from '@gntik-ai/chat';

const adapter = createEchoAdapter();

/** A backend-free, keyboard-accessible echo conversation with Stop and Retry. */
export default function UseChatEcho() {
  const { messages, isStreaming, sendMessage, stop, regenerate, error } = useChat({ adapter });
  const lastReply = [...messages]
    .reverse()
    .find((m) => m.role === 'assistant' && m.status === 'done')
    ?.parts.filter((p) => p.type === 'text')
    .map((p) => p.text)
    .join('');
  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-2xl flex-col gap-4">
      {messages.map((message) => {
        const text = message.parts
          .filter((p) => p.type === 'text')
          .map((p) => p.text)
          .join('');
        const streaming = message.status === 'pending' || message.status === 'streaming';
        return (
          <ChatMessage
            key={message.id}
            role={message.role}
            streaming={streaming}
            copyText={text}
            onRetry={message.role === 'assistant' && !isStreaming ? () => regenerate(message.id) : undefined}
          >
            {text && <Markdown streaming={streaming}>{text}</Markdown>}
          </ChatMessage>
        );
      })}
      {error && (
        <p role="alert" className="text-destructive-text">
          {error.message}
        </p>
      )}
      <ChatComposer onSubmit={sendMessage} streaming={isStreaming} onStop={stop} />
      <ChatAnnouncer streaming={isStreaming} lastReply={lastReply} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### useConversations (`use-conversations`)

Experimental local conversation state beside useChat. ChatConversation reuses ConversationSummary (id, title, required updatedAt, preview, unread, icon, disabled) plus optional metadata. Options: defaultConversations (empty), defaultActiveId (null), controlled activeId, onActiveChange(id | null), onConversationsChange(list). Returns conversations, activeId, setActiveId, addConversation(item, placement?), setConversation(id, patch | updater), removeConversation, getConversation, setConversations, getMessages and setMessages. Add prepends by default, append opts out, duplicates return false. Patches cannot change id; unknown ids are ignored. Removal selects the next item, then previous, then null; controlled ids pass through unchanged until the prop changes, even when absent from the list. List and selection callbacks run once per change, never on mount. getMessages is not reactive: setMessages stores an array by reference without rendering; missing ids share a frozen empty array. Render previews from preview and updatedAt, and supply timestamps yourself. Removal drops stored messages. Each hook instance is independent; persistence belongs to the product. The echo example shows adding, renaming, removing, switching and restoring histories. Its owning-id ref skips stale write-back during the useChat id-reset effect.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/chat` · export `useConversations` · group Feedback · status experimental
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/chat/src/useConversations/useConversations.doc.ts
- Registry dependencies: conversation-list, use-chat
- Install: `gntik-ui add use-conversations`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject use-conversations`

Usage:

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { Button, Input } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { ChatComposer } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { ChatAnnouncer, ChatMessage } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { Markdown } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { createEchoAdapter, useChat } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { useConversations, type ChatConversation } from '@gntik-ai/chat';

const adapter = createEchoAdapter();
const initial: ChatConversation[] = [
  { id: 'c1', title: 'First chat', updatedAt: '2026-11-01' },
  { id: 'c2', title: 'Second chat', updatedAt: '2026-11-01' },
];

/** Local histories; persistence belongs to the product. */
export default function UseConversationsEcho() {
  const {
    conversations,
    activeId,
    setActiveId,
    addConversation,
    setConversation,
    removeConversation,
    getMessages,
    setMessages,
  } = useConversations({ defaultConversations: initial, defaultActiveId: 'c1' });
  const nextId = useRef(3);
  const { messages, isStreaming, sendMessage, stop, error } = useChat({
    adapter,
    id: activeId ?? undefined,
    initialMessages: activeId === null ? undefined : getMessages(activeId),
  });
  const owningId = useRef(activeId);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (owningId.current !== activeId) {
      // useChat resets in an effect: this render still contains the previous id's messages.
      owningId.current = activeId;
      return;
    }
    if (activeId !== null) setMessages(activeId, messages);
  }, [activeId, messages, setMessages]);

  const selected = conversations.find((item) => item.id === activeId);
  const lastReply = messages
    .filter((message) => message.role === 'assistant')
    .at(-1)
    ?.parts.filter((part) => part.type === 'text')
    .map((part) => part.text)
    .join('');

  return (
    <div className="flex max-w-2xl flex-col gap-4">
      <nav aria-label="Conversations">
        <ul className="flex flex-wrap gap-2">
          {conversations.map((conversation) => (
            <li key={conversation.id}>
              <Button
                variant="secondary"
                aria-pressed={activeId === conversation.id}
                onClick={() => setActiveId(conversation.id)}
              >
                {conversation.title}
              </Button>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      </nav>
      <Button
        variant="secondary"
        onClick={() => {
          const number = nextId.current++;
          const id = `c${number}`;
          addConversation({ id, title: `Chat ${number}`, updatedAt: new Date() });
          setActiveId(id);
        }}
      >
        New chat
      </Button>
      {selected ? (
        <>
          <Input
            aria-label="Conversation title"
            value={selected.title}
            onValueChange={(title) => setConversation(selected.id, { title, updatedAt: new Date() })}
          />
          <Button variant="secondary" onClick={() => removeConversation(selected.id)}>
            Remove chat
          </Button>
          <section aria-label="Messages" className="flex flex-col gap-4">
            {messages.map((message) => {
              const text = message.parts
                .filter((part) => part.type === 'text')
                .map((part) => part.text)
                .join('');
              const streaming = message.status === 'pending' || message.status === 'streaming';
              return (
                <ChatMessage key={message.id} role={message.role} streaming={streaming} copyText={text}>
                  {text && <Markdown streaming={streaming}>{text}</Markdown>}
                </ChatMessage>
              );
            })}
          </section>
          {error && (
            <p role="alert" className="text-destructive-text">
              {error.message}
            </p>
          )}
          <ChatComposer key={activeId} onSubmit={sendMessage} streaming={isStreaming} onStop={stop} />
          <ChatAnnouncer streaming={isStreaming} lastReply={lastReply} />
        </>
      ) : (
        <p className="text-muted-foreground">Create a conversation to start chatting.</p>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Calendar (`calendar`)

The public localeWeekStart(locale?) helper returns the locale first weekday (0–6, Monday fallback), matching scheduling blocks. Day or range selection with one or two months, inclusive min/max bounds and Intl names. The clickable month heading opens a month grid, then the year heading opens a shared 12-year page (2020–2031 for 2026). Set maxView="day" for the previous static header, or "month" to stop at months; the default is "year". Optional view/defaultView/onViewChange control or report the view (initially "day"). captionLayout="select" uses labelled kit month/year selects; yearRange={from,to} defaults to the current year ±10, clipped to min/max and including the visible year. Picking a month returns to days, preserving and clamping the focused day, and calls onMonthChange once with the first day. DatePicker and DateRangePicker forward maxView and captionLayout and reopen in the day view.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Calendar` · group Forms · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Calendar/Calendar.doc.ts
- ARIA pattern: grid (date picker dialog calendar)
- Registry dependencies: select, ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add calendar`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject calendar`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Day: ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Moves focus to the previous / next day (reversed in RTL) |
| Day: ArrowUp / ArrowDown | Moves focus to the same day in the previous / next week |
| Day: PageUp / PageDown | Moves focus to the same day in the previous / next month (Shift: year) |
| Day: Home / End | Moves focus to the first / last day of the week |
| Day: Enter / Space | Selects the focused day (range: first press sets the start, second the end) |
| Month: ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Moves one month (reversed in RTL) |
| Month: ArrowUp / ArrowDown | Moves three months |
| Month: Home / End | Moves to the first / last month of the row |
| Month: PageUp / PageDown | Moves one year |
| Month: Enter / Space | Opens the day view of the focused month; disabled months do nothing |
| Year: ArrowLeft / ArrowRight | Moves one year (reversed in RTL) |
| Year: ArrowUp / ArrowDown | Moves three years |
| Year: Home / End | Moves to the first / last year of the row |
| Year: PageUp / PageDown | Moves twelve years |
| Year: Enter / Space | Opens the month view of the focused year; disabled years do nothing |
| Heading: Enter / Space | Opens the month view, then year view, up to maxView |
| Popup: Escape | Closes the date picker and returns focus to its field from any view |

Tokens: foreground, muted-foreground, primary, primary-foreground, secondary, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { I18nProvider, localeWeekStart, useI18n } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { Calendar } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

function LocaleCalendar() {
  const { locale, t } = useI18n();
  return (
    <Calendar
      aria-label={`${t('calendar.label')} (${locale})`}
      defaultMonth={new Date(2026, 3, 1)}
      weekStartsOn={localeWeekStart(locale)}
    />
  );
}

/** The exported helper matches the Calendar and scheduling defaults. */
export default function CalendarLocale() {
  return (
    <div className="flex flex-wrap gap-6">
      {['en-US', 'es-ES'].map((locale) => (
        <I18nProvider key={locale} locale={locale}>
          <LocaleCalendar />
        </I18nProvider>
      ))}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### ChatComposer (`chat-composer`)

Chat input with autosizing text, validated attachments, a model picker, tools, a counter and streaming Stop. Optional submitMode="mod+enter" lets Enter add a line and Ctrl/Meta+Enter send; the default remains Enter to send. Both modes ignore IME composition. header renders above attachments (use ChatComposerHeader with title, optional onClose and children); prefix sits at the inline start of the text row, following LTR/RTL direction; footer sits below the toolbar and above the hint. readOnly keeps text focusable and selectable without dimming, disables sending and hides attachment editing; Stop still works. actionsRef exposes focus(start/end/all), insert(text, cursor/start/end), clear() and getValue(); the normal ref still points to the textarea. insert replaces the selection and restores the caret after rendering: controlled parents must apply onValueChange synchronously (debounced updates can lose the caret). clear removes text only, keeping attachments. With none of the new props set, the DOM and keyboard behavior are unchanged. Examples show quote reply with a header and one chip, text actions, multiline submission and read-only drafts.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/chat` · export `ChatComposer` · group Forms · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/chat/src/ChatComposer/ChatComposer.doc.ts
- Registry dependencies: attachment
- Install: `gntik-ui add chat-composer`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject chat-composer`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Enter (submitMode=enter, default) | Sends the message (ignored while streaming, read-only or during IME composition) |
| Shift+Enter | Inserts a new line |
| Enter (submitMode=mod+enter) | Inserts a new line |
| Ctrl+Enter / Meta+Enter (submitMode=mod+enter) | Sends once (both modifiers work on every platform; ignored during IME composition, streaming or read-only) |
| Escape | While a reply streams: stops it |
| Tab | Moves through the header, attachment Retry/Remove buttons, the text box, attach, tools, the model picker and Send/Stop |
| Ctrl/⌘+V | In the text box: pasted files are attached (validated) instead of inserted |

Tokens: card, destructive-chip-text, primary-text, border, primary, ring, secondary, muted-foreground, destructive-text, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
import { ModelPicker, DEMO_MODELS } from '@gntik-ai/chat';
import { ChatComposer, type ComposerAttachment } from '@gntik-ai/chat';

let seq = 0;

export default function ChatComposerFull() {
  const [model, setModel] = useState<string | null>('balanced');
  const [files, setFiles] = useState<ComposerAttachment[]>([
    { id: 'f1', name: 'invoices-september.csv', size: 48_213, type: 'text/csv' },
    { id: 'f2', name: 'release-notes.md', size: 9_042, error: 'Network error' },
  ]);
  const [sent, setSent] = useState<string[]>([]);
  const timers = useRef<Array<ReturnType<typeof setInterval>>>([]);
  const urls = useRef<string[]>([]);

  useEffect(
    () => () => {
      timers.current.forEach(clearInterval);
      urls.current.forEach((u) => URL.revokeObjectURL?.(u));
    },
    [],
  );

  // Mock upload: progress ticks to 100.
  const upload = (id: string) => {
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      setFiles((all) =>
        all.map((f) => {
          if (f.id !== id) return f;
          const progress = Math.min(100, (f.progress ?? 0) + 20);
          if (progress >= 100) clearInterval(timer);
          return { ...f, progress };
        }),
      );
    }, 300);
    timers.current.push(timer);
  };

  const attach = (picked: File[]) => {
    const added = picked.map((p) => {
      const id = `file-${++seq}`;
      const previewUrl =
        p.type.startsWith('image/') && typeof URL.createObjectURL === 'function' ? URL.createObjectURL(p) : undefined;
      if (previewUrl) urls.current.push(previewUrl);
      return { id, name: p.name, size: p.size, type: p.type, previewUrl, progress: 0 };
    });
    setFiles((f) => [...f, ...added]);
    added.forEach((a) => upload(a.id));
  };

  return (
    <div className="max-w-2xl">
      <ChatComposer
        maxLength={2000}
        attachments={files}
        accept=".pdf,.csv,.md,.txt,image/*"
        maxSize={10_000_000}
        maxFiles={5}
        onAttach={attach}
        onRemoveAttachment={(id) => setFiles((f) => f.filter((x) => x.id !== id))}
        onRetryAttachment={(id) => {
          setFiles((f) => f.map((x) => (x.id === id ? { ...x, error: undefined, progress: 0 } : x)));
          upload(id);
        }}
        modelPicker={<ModelPicker compact models={DEMO_MODELS} value={model} onValueChange={setModel} />}
        onSubmit={(text) => {
          setSent((s) => [text, ...s].slice(0, 3));
          setFiles([]);
        }}
      />
      {sent.length > 0 && (
        <ul aria-label="Sent messages" className="mt-3 space-y-1 text-[12.5px] text-muted-foreground">
          {sent.map((t, i) => (
            <li key={i}>Sent: {t}</li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```

### Checkbox (`checkbox`)

Checkbox with optional label and description, including the indeterminate state. CheckboxGroup shares state across several checkboxes (plain or bordered list layout) and supports a parent "select all" checkbox. An explicit aria-label takes precedence over the visible label; keep both consistent for WCAG 2.5.3 (label in name).

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `Checkbox` · group Forms · status stable
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/ui/src/components/Checkbox/Checkbox.doc.ts
- Primitive: `@base-ui/react/checkbox, @base-ui/react/checkbox-group`
- ARIA pattern: checkbox (dual and mixed state)
- Registry dependencies: ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add checkbox`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject checkbox`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Space | Toggles the focused checkbox; a parent checkbox ticks or clears the whole group |
| Tab | Moves focus to the next checkbox (each checkbox is a tab stop) |

Tokens: background, border, primary, primary-foreground, foreground, muted-foreground, destructive, focus-ring

Usage:

```tsx
import { useId, useState } from 'react';
import { Checkbox, CheckboxGroup } from '@gntik-ai/ui';

const OPTIONS = [
  { value: 'mentions', label: 'Mentions', description: 'When someone mentions you in a comment or review.' },
  { value: 'deployments', label: 'Deployments', description: 'When a deployment you own succeeds or fails.' },
  { value: 'billing', label: 'Billing', description: 'Invoices, failed payments and plan changes.' },
];

export default function CheckboxList() {
  const [value, setValue] = useState(['mentions', 'deployments']);
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="grid max-w-lg gap-6">
      <div>
        <div id={id} className="mb-3 text-[13px] font-semibold text-foreground">
          Email notifications
        </div>
        <CheckboxGroup aria-labelledby={id} variant="list" value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
          {OPTIONS.map((o) => (
            <Checkbox key={o.value} name="notifications" value={o.value} label={o.label} description={o.description} />
          ))}
        </CheckboxGroup>
      </div>
      <Checkbox label="I agree to the terms of service" defaultChecked />
      <Checkbox label="Archived projects (locked)" disabled />
    </div>
  );
}
```

### ChoiceCard (`choice-card`)

Cards as controls. ClickableCard: the whole card is one link or button (a stretched title, so there is a single focus target with a short name) with icon, description, meta and a chevron. SelectableCard inside SelectableCardGroup: option cards with radio (single) or checkbox (multiple) semantics on Base UI RadioGroup / CheckboxGroup, with a check indicator, title, description, meta and disabled state.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/ui` · export `ChoiceCard` · group Forms · status beta

- ARIA pattern: link / button · radiogroup · group of checkboxes
- Registry dependencies: ui-utils
- Install: `gntik-ui add choice-card`; own the source with `gntik-ui eject choice-card`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | ClickableCard: focuses its link or button. Group: enters the radio group once, on the selected card; visits each checkbox card |
| Enter | Activates a ClickableCard |
| Arrow keys | Radio group: move to the next / previous card and select it |
| Space | Checkbox group: toggles the focused card (radio: selects it) |

Tokens: background, border, secondary, foreground, muted-foreground, primary, primary-foreground, focus-ring

        chevron={false}
