### Page header (`page-header`)

Screen header with breadcrumb, title and status, description, meta row, actions that fold into a MoreMenu on small screens, and optional navigation tabs. titleRef targets the h1 for titleRef.current.focus(), adding tabIndex=-1 only when supplied so the title stays outside the Tab order. In a StatusLayout heading slot use as="div" and disable breadcrumb, meta, tabs, actions, status and description fixtures; the slot supplies the page’s only h1. The tablist name follows I18nProvider (en/es); the Spanish preview keeps caller content unchanged. Optional labels?: Partial<PageHeaderLabels> overrides each built-in label. Explicit content props win over labels, then I18nProvider (en/es); no provider keeps English. Imported fixtures and machine data stay unchanged. See the Catalog labels live preview. wrapTitle?: boolean (default false) wraps the full title, including long words, while preserving titleRef focus behavior. The default title remains truncated. See the Spanish live preview for a wrapping title.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/blocks` · export `PageHeader` · group page-chrome · status beta

### Cursor pager footer (`cursor-pager-footer`)

Responsive stateless cursor-pagination footer for data-table paginated={false}. Forwards CursorPaginationProps: hasPrevious, hasNext, onPrevious, onNext, loading, busy, summary, shownCount, total, unavailableBehaviour, pageSize, pageSizeOptions, onPageSizeChange, previousLabel, nextLabel, ariaLabel, loadingLabel, labels and className. Consumer-owned opaque cursors stay outside the kit. summary accepts plain text or null; the count form requires labels.shownSummary and labels.totalSummary; select options require labels.rowsPerPage and labels.rowsPerPageLabel. Flat names override labels.previous, labels.next and labels.navLabel, then catalog defaults. loadingLabel=null preserves the summary while busy. One persistent polite atomic status; buttons remain focusable when aria-disabled. Removal of a focused control moves focus to Next, Previous, select, then nav root, including while busy. No page numbers or ranges. No props renders fixtures.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/blocks` · export `CursorPagerFooter` · group tables · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/blocks/src/tables/CursorPagerFooter/block.meta.ts
- Composes: CursorPagination
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=block&id=cursor-pager-footer
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/blocks`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add cursor-pager-footer`

Labels (optional Partial per instance; explicit keys override provider translations and defaults):

| Key | Type | State / surface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `previous` | `string` | Previous name, below previousLabel and above catalog defaults |
| `next` | `string` | Next name, below nextLabel and above catalog defaults |
| `navLabel` | `string` | Navigation name, below ariaLabel and above catalog defaults |
| `shownSummary` | `(shownCount: number) => string` | Required in count form: no positive exact total |
| `totalSummary` | `(total: number) => string` | Required in count form: positive exact total |
| `rowsPerPage` | `string` | Required with pageSizeOptions: visible select label |
| `rowsPerPageLabel` | `string` | Required with pageSizeOptions: select accessible name |

Usage:

```tsx

// Props default to the block fixtures; pass your data.

```

### Data table (`data-table`)

Opt-in csvExport adds an Export menu: All rows in current sort order across pages (before grouping), Current page in grouped display order, Selected rows and Copy selected rows (also Ctrl/Cmd+C on non-editable table content without a document text selection). csvExport accepts fileName and scopes (rows/page/selected). The filename defaults to the slugged caption, or table.csv without a supplied caption. Visible exportable columns keep display order; exportValue overrides accessor (nullish results fall back), columns without either are omitted, and exportable=false opts out. Values stay raw: ISO dates, booleans, numbers and empty null cells. CSV includes a BOM; CSV and clipboard TSV both use shared toCsv formula protection for headers and values. Single selection exports selectedId; multiple selection resolves include/exclude models across loaded rows. onExport receives scope, exported column ids, selected ids, sort and opaque filters; while pending the trigger stays focusable and busy and repeat exports are ignored. Use onExport for large result sets, and handle errors in the callback. Server pagination requires onExport and labels All rows with rowCount; clipboard copying and its shortcut are unavailable in server mode because unloaded selections cannot be copied completely. See examples/csv-export.tsx for client, delegated server and single-row previews. Generic typed table: sortable headers with aria-sort, row selection with select-all and indeterminate by default (selectionMode="multiple"), selectionMode="none" to hide selection, column visibility menu, density toggle, row actions, loading and empty states, client-side sort and pagination, optional row groups (groupBy) with rowgroup header rows, counts, keyboard-accessible collapse buttons and group selection; column resize (pointer drag or a focusable role="separator" handle with arrow keys, min/max widths, controlled columnWidths), column pinning to either edge with sticky cells (column menu or pinnedColumns), row virtualization for large datasets (aria-rowcount/aria-rowindex, works with selection and grouping), inline cell editing (text, number and select editors; Enter/F2 to edit, Enter/Tab to commit, Escape to cancel, onCellEdit can reject with an inline error) and saved views (filters, sort, visible columns, widths, pinning and grouping) with a view switcher to save as, rename, delete and reset. Opt-in selectionMode="single" uses native radios in a labelled fieldset (never virtualized; client pagination defaults to false, and paginated=true or paginationMode="server" enables pagination). Single mode uses selectedId/onSelectedIdChange or defaultSelectedId; isRowDisabled skips unavailable rows and preserves a checked disabled choice without callbacks. Supply legend, aria-label or aria-labelledby for the group and getRowLabel for each radio (otherwise the first column labels it). selectionName is used verbatim and must be unique per page; omitted names use an instance-unique useId name, and duplicate supplied names or missing group labels warn in development. Tab enters once on the checked enabled row or first enabled row; arrows wrap and skip disabled rows, Space selects, Shift+Tab exits, and all-disabled groups have no tab stop. No select-all, group checkboxes, bulk actions or selection summary appear in single mode. Examples in examples/single-selection.tsx: an uncontrolled non-paginated list with legend="Available items" and a controlled versions table with legend="Available versions", selectedId="v2" and a checked disabled version. Opt-in paginationMode="server" accepts a controlled 1-based page, pageSize and required rowCount (known total), with onPageChange/onPageSizeChange requests. Supplied rows render in order without client sorting or slicing. Sortable columns show sort buttons and aria-sort when onSortChange or onQueryChange is supplied; without either, headers stay plain. Sorting toggles ascending/descending, updates uncontrolled sort (controlled sort waits for the prop), and requests page 1 when not already there. aria-sort reflects the requested order before rows arrive; reset controlled sort to the last confirmed order if a request fails. Saved views restore changed sort and request page 1; views that only change filters keep the current server page. Clearing sort is reported as null through onQueryChange, since onSortChange accepts only a non-null SortState. Single selection keeps its chosen id across pages. Off-page choices leave every visible radio unchecked and the first enabled radio is the tab stop; name the current choice in the legend. See examples/paginated-single-selection.tsx for client and server pagination. The footer stays visible for empty results, clamps stale pages for display without callbacks, and hides during loading. Page-size changes may also request a page to keep the first visible row on screen. The consumer owns fetching and reconciles stale pages. onQueryChange receives one synchronous DataTableQuery per user page, pageSize, sort or view action in both modes: { page, pageSize, sort, filters, cause }. It includes the next page and size together on resize, and the restored filters on a view; consumer filter prop changes do not emit queries. Use onQueryChange OR the separate callbacks for fetching to avoid duplicate requests; existing callbacks retain their order and arguments. See examples/server-pagination.tsx for sortable columns and one request per query, with controlled sort reset on failure. Multiple selection preserves ids from other server pages by default; preserveSelection=false restores page-only reporting, and client tables can opt in with preserveSelection=true. selectedIds remains supported. A controlled selectionModel takes precedence and uses { type: "include", ids: string[] } for selected ids or { type: "exclude", ids: string[] } for every match except those ids. bulkActions(ids, model) receives the full include list; in exclude mode ids contains enabled selections in the current rows and the model is authoritative. One-argument actions remain compatible. selectAllMatching defaults to false and offers a strip after the page is fully selected: client mode includes every enabled row, while server mode requires onSelectionModelChange and reports an exclude model. The same button becomes Clear selection without moving focus; clearing returns focus to the page checkbox, or to the table when the checkbox is hidden or unavailable. An exclude model resets through both callbacks when filters changes by JSON value; filters must include every narrowing input, including search text. Paging, page size and sorting preserve selection. An exclude action covers the matching result set at action time, including later-created rows; the consumer executes it. isRowDisabled disables multiple-selection checkboxes and page/group/all-matching toggles skip known disabled rows. Server counts use rowCount minus explicit excluded ids, including disabled ids on the page where Select all is activated. isRowDisabled cannot evaluate unloaded rows, so the server must enforce eligibility for the complete matching result set; return only eligible matches and their rowCount when counts must exclude all unavailable rows. hideSelectAll defaults to false and hides just the header checkbox, retaining an accessible Selection heading. See examples/client-selection.tsx for client preservation, disabled rows and select-all-matching, and examples/server-pagination.tsx for controlled models, cross-page actions and the preservation/header options.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/blocks` · export `DataTable` · group tables · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/blocks/src/tables/DataTable/block.meta.ts
- Composes: Table, Checkbox, Menu, MoreMenu, ToggleGroup, Button, Skeleton, EmptyState, Pagination, SimpleSelect, StatusTag, Input, Dialog
- Registry dependencies: pagination-footer
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=block&id=data-table
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/blocks`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add data-table`

### Load more footer (`load-more-footer`)

A load more button and loaded-count summary for appended lists without a total or page count. Cursor mode uses nextCursor and optional hasMore; flag mode omits nextCursor and uses hasMore. Compose with DataTable paginated={false} or Collapsible and JsonViewer cards. The consumer owns rows, filters and cursor normalization. Each attempt must settle loading=false together with its result in one update; split settles are unsupported. Keep cursor, hasMore, counts and lastAppend unchanged on failure. Cursor failures replace the button with ErrorPanel; flag failures keep the same button. Exhaustion removes every control even on failure. Focus moves only when the focused control is removed, to its replacement or exhaustedFocusTarget (summary by default, root optionally). lastAppend uses increasing seq values for successful appends, never initial loads, replacements or failures. New appended counts are announced politely; settled errors assertively. Self-wraps in LiveAnnouncer when needed. Every label has translated defaults and per-key overrides.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/blocks` · export `LoadMoreFooter` · group tables · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/blocks/src/tables/LoadMoreFooter/block.meta.ts
- Composes: Button, ErrorPanel, LiveAnnouncer
- Registry dependencies: error-panel
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=block&id=load-more-footer
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/blocks`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add load-more-footer`

Labels (optional Partial per instance; explicit keys override provider translations and defaults):

| Key | Type | State / surface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `loadMore` | `string` | Available and idle: button name |
| `loading` | `string` | Loading: button name; ErrorPanel uses its own translated busy text |
| `retry` | `string` | Failed and available: retry button name |
| `group` | `string` | Always: root group accessible name |
| `moreAvailable` | `string` | Available: visible summary note |
| `summary` | `(count: number) => string` | Always: loaded-count summary and default exhaustion focus target |
| `loadedAnnouncement` | `(count: number) => string` | New lastAppend.seq with positive count: polite announcement |

Usage:

```tsx
import { LoadMoreFooter } from '@gntik-ai/blocks';

// Props default to the block fixtures; pass your data.
<LoadMoreFooter />
```

### Subordinate list (`subordinate-list`)

Read-only list section inside a resource-form host, composing section-header, data-table, pagination-footer, empty-states, skeletons and error-panel. All props are required: title (string), headingLevel (h2 or h3), count (number, including 0), columns (typed DataTableColumn<T>[]), rows (readonly T[]), getRowId, pagination ({limit, offset, total, onPageChange(offset)} or null), loading (boolean), error ({title, message, code: string | number | null} or null), onRetry and emptyState (host-supplied ReactNode). Every supplied row renders; server pagination converts the zero-based offset to a 1-based footer page and fixes pageSizeOptions to [limit]. No filtering, sorting, selection, create action, toolbar, virtualization, pinning or sticky region. Error takes precedence over loading, then empty and data; retry uses the current i18n locale. Error headings use h3 for either section heading level. Composition example: packages/blocks/src/tables/SubordinateList/examples/ResourceForm.tsx uses the resource-form form sections and sticky save bar with a server-paginated History section and an unpaginated Consumers section.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/blocks` · export `SubordinateList` · group tables · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/blocks/src/tables/SubordinateList/block.meta.ts
- Composes: section-header, data-table, pagination-footer, empty-states, skeletons, error-panel
- Registry dependencies: data-table, error-panel, pagination-footer, section-header, skeletons
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=block&id=subordinate-list
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/blocks`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add subordinate-list`

Usage:

```tsx
import { Field, FieldLabel, Input, Page, Stack } from '@gntik-ai/ui';
import { useState } from 'react';
import { FormSection } from '@gntik-ai/blocks';
import { NoResultsEmpty } from '@gntik-ai/blocks';
import { StickyActionBar } from '@gntik-ai/blocks';
import { SubordinateList } from '@gntik-ai/blocks';
import type { DataTableColumn } from '@gntik-ai/blocks';

interface RecordRow {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  status: string;
}
const columns: DataTableColumn<RecordRow>[] = [
  { id: 'name', header: 'Name', accessor: (row) => row.name },
  { id: 'status', header: 'Status', accessor: (row) => row.status },
];
const history: RecordRow[] = Array.from({ length: 37 }, (_, i) => ({
  id: `record-${i}`,
  name: `Revision ${i + 1}`,
  status: 'Completed',
}));
const consumers: RecordRow[] = [
  { id: 'worker', name: 'Worker', status: 'Current' },
  { id: 'scheduler', name: 'Scheduler', status: 'Current' },
];

export type ExampleState = 'default' | 'loading' | 'empty' | 'error';

/** A resource-form host owns the form and sticky save bar; its two lists load independently. */
export default function ResourceFormExample({ state = 'default' }: { state?: ExampleState }) {
  const [name, setName] = useState('Shared resource');
  const [savedName, setSavedName] = useState(name);
  const [offset, setOffset] = useState(0);
  const [failed, setFailed] = useState(state === 'error');
  return (
    <Page title="Resource settings" description="Edit a resource and review its related records.">
      <form
        aria-label="Resource settings"
        onSubmit={(event) => {
          event.preventDefault();
          setSavedName(name);
        }}
      >
        <Stack gap={8}>
          <FormSection
            title="General"
            description="Settings for this resource."
            actions={null}
            headingLevel="h2"
            divided={false}
          >
            <Field>
              <FieldLabel>Resource name</FieldLabel>
              <Input value={name} onValueChange={setName} />
            </Field>
          </FormSection>
          <SubordinateList
            title="History"
            headingLevel="h2"
            count={state === 'empty' ? 0 : history.length}
            columns={columns}
            rows={state === 'empty' ? [] : history.slice(offset, offset + 10)}
            getRowId={(row) => row.id}
            pagination={{
              limit: 10,
              offset,
              total: state === 'empty' ? 0 : history.length,
              onPageChange: setOffset,
            }}
            loading={state === 'loading'}
            error={
              failed
                ? {
                    title: 'History unavailable',
                    message: 'Please retry to load the history.',
                    code: null,
                  }
                : null
            }
            onRetry={() => setFailed(false)}
            emptyState={
              <NoResultsEmpty
                query=""
                filterCount={0}
                entity="history records"
                titleAs="h3"
                bordered={true}
                className=""
                onClearFilters={() => {}}
                onClearSearch={() => {}}
              />
            }
          />
          <SubordinateList
            title="Consumers"
            headingLevel="h2"
            count={consumers.length}
            columns={columns}
            rows={consumers}
            getRowId={(row) => row.id}
            pagination={null}
            loading={false}
            error={null}
            onRetry={() => {}}
            emptyState={
              <NoResultsEmpty
                query=""
                filterCount={0}
                entity="consumers"
                titleAs="h3"
                bordered={true}
                className=""
                onClearFilters={() => {}}
                onClearSearch={() => {}}
              />
            }
          />
          <StickyActionBar
            dirty={name !== savedName}
            saving={false}
            onSave={() => setSavedName(name)}
            onCancel={() => setName(savedName)}
          />
        </Stack>
      </form>
    </Page>
  );
}
```

### Truncated collection footer (`truncated-collection-footer`)

Presentation-only summary of a loaded first cursor page without a total or pager. N+ is a lower bound when hasMore is true; the note explains that more items exist. Compose below data-table (DataTable with paginated={false}). First-page recipe: use hasMore={true} for N+ plus a note, and supply noteId so a consumer table can reference it with aria-describedby. DataTable does not forward aria-describedby; its named containing region can reference the note instead. Count-only recipe: use hasMore={false} for the visible count without a note. PageToolbar has no count prop; this block carries the count. No navigation or focusable elements. Every visible string is overridable through noun, summaryLabel, formatCount and truncationNote; ReactNode overrides must remain plain text without interactive or hidden content. The i18n provider supplies translated defaults; locale overrides number formatting. Required inputs are visibleCount and hasMore, with meaningful runtime defaults for the JavaScript catalogue preview.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/blocks` · export `TruncatedCollectionFooter` · group tables · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/blocks/src/tables/TruncatedCollectionFooter/block.meta.ts
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=block&id=truncated-collection-footer
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/blocks`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add truncated-collection-footer`

Usage:

```tsx
import { TruncatedCollectionFooter } from '@gntik-ai/blocks';

/** Count-only recipe: retain the visible count without introducing truncation messaging. */
export default function ExactExample() {
  return <TruncatedCollectionFooter visibleCount={37} hasMore={false} noun="records" />;
}
```

### Forgot password (`forgot-password`)

Centred card recovery with default email, inbox feedback and resend. Supports identifier (type, autoComplete, label, help/helpId, placeholder, minLength/maxLength), messages (identifierRequired/identifierInvalid/identifierTooShort/passwordRequired), and React 19 ref.focus. The kit owns inline validation and focuses the first invalid field; consumers supply messages, not a second inline validator. Server errors use error + fieldInvalid + feedbackId; aria-describedby describes the form, while flagged inputs also retain their help and error ids. headingLevel (h1/h2/h3/null) suppresses the heading without losing the form name; aria-label/aria-labelledby override the default name. Forwards ForgotPasswordForm props unchanged, including ref.focus(identifier), title/description, sentTitle/sentDescription, sentStatus and resendActions (null hides sent copy or actions). suppressAllHeadings suppresses headings in request and sent states. footer accepts replacement content or null. Preview: forgot-password--username-or-email.

### Public hub (`public-hub`)

Unauthenticated entry hub on AuthLayout full-bleed with PageHeader, explanatory cards and navigation actions. Use public-hub instead of landing for an account entry point without a marketing hero or screenshot; use sign-in-card for a single sign-in form. Recommend 2 to 4 cards; any number is supported. Cards use the kit sm breakpoint: one column below sm, two from sm. ARIA: a section labelled by the text span inside the single PageHeader h1, h2 card headings and a ul/li card list. The title span owns the aria-labelledby target id in server HTML and after hydration; PageHeader has no heading-id prop. Loading replaces content with decorative kit Skeletons in an aria-busy section named by loadingLabel. Keyboard: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the primary, secondary and tertiary links in visual order; Enter follows href and invokes onClick, with visible focus and no trap. AuthLayout retains its skip link, named "Skip to main content", before the content in both states. The PageHeader title inherits truncation for long titles.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default / behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| eyebrow | string | Omitted; optional Badge before PageHeader |
| title | string | Welcome; PageHeader h1 |
| description | string | Omitted; PageHeader description |
| cards | { title: string; body: string }[] | Omitted; explanatory list with h2 headings |
| primaryAction | { label: string; href: string; onClick?: MouseEventHandler<HTMLAnchorElement> } | Sign in, #sign-in; Button rendered as an anchor |
| secondaryAction | Same action shape | Omitted; secondary Button rendered as an anchor |
| tertiaryLink | Same action shape | Omitted; one kit Link |
| footer | string | Omitted; Separator then supporting Text |
| loading | boolean | false; replaces header, cards and actions; hides eyebrow/footer copy |
| logo | ReactNode | Active preset logo from AuthLayout |
| loadingLabel | string | Loading; accessible name of the busy section |

Optional content has no default fixtures and creates no empty wrappers; an empty cards array also renders no list. Without footer there is no separator. Preview fixtures: public-hub--full, public-hub--minimal, public-hub--loading and public-hub--minimal-loading.

## Theme examples

Import ThemeProvider from @gntik-ai/ui and PublicHubPage from @gntik-ai/templates. Pass account routes and copy as props. Each theme supports the same full, minimal and loading composition.

```tsx
<ThemeProvider defaultMode="dark" storageKey={null}>
  <PublicHubPage title="Welcome" primaryAction={{ label: 'Sign in', href: '/sign-in' }} />
</ThemeProvider>
```

```tsx
<ThemeProvider defaultMode="light" storageKey={null}>
  <PublicHubPage title="Welcome" primaryAction={{ label: 'Sign in', href: '/sign-in' }} />
</ThemeProvider>
```

```tsx
<ThemeProvider defaultMode="high_contrast" storageKey={null}>
  <PublicHubPage title="Welcome" primaryAction={{ label: 'Sign in', href: '/sign-in' }} />
</ThemeProvider>
```

- Package: `@gntik-ai/templates` · export `PublicHubPage` · group Auth · status stable
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/templates/src/public-hub/template.meta.ts
- ARIA pattern: Named section (aria-labelledby points to the title span inside the PageHeader h1, including in server HTML); h2 card headings in a ul/li list. Loading: aria-busy=true and aria-label=loadingLabel, with decorative Skeletons and no content links or headings.
- Layout: AuthLayout
- Blocks: page-header
- Console shell: no
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=template&id=public-hub

### Sign in (card) (`sign-in-card`)

Centred card sign-in with default email and password, legal footer and no SSO. Supports identifier (type, autoComplete, label, help/helpId, placeholder, minLength/maxLength), messages (identifierRequired/identifierInvalid/identifierTooShort/passwordRequired), and React 19 ref.focus. The kit owns inline validation and focuses the first invalid field; consumers supply messages, not a second inline validator. Server errors use error + fieldInvalid + feedbackId; aria-describedby describes the form, while flagged inputs also retain their help and error ids. headingLevel (h1/h2/h3/null) suppresses the heading without losing the form name; aria-label/aria-labelledby override the default name. Forwards SignInForm props unchanged, including passwordHelp/passwordHelpId and ref.focus(identifier/password). Text submissions retain email and add identifier. suppressAllHeadings suppresses every internal heading. footer, sso and signUpPrompt accept replacements or null. Preview: sign-in-card--username.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/templates` · export `SignInCardPage` · group Auth · status stable
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/templates/src/sign-in-card/template.meta.ts
- Layout: AuthLayout
- Blocks: sign-in-form
- Console shell: no
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=template&id=sign-in-card
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/templates`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add sign-in-card`

### Flow builder (`workflow-builder`)

onSave(graph) receives the graph on screen (controlled graph, latest reported edit, or initial starter graph), without selected, dragging or measured node fields. Zero-argument handlers remain valid. Optional graph and onGraphChange pass through to FlowBuilder. Committed edits show actionBar.unsaved, a resolved save shows actionBar.saved, and a rejected save retains unsaved status and releases loading. Edits during a pending save remain unsaved. examples/SaveGraph.tsx shows a controlled graph and onSave={(graph) => localStorage.setItem("workflow-builder-example", JSON.stringify(graph))}; hosts own persistence. Full-screen workflow editor with optional nodeTypes, onConnectEdge, onConnect, isValidConnection, onConnectionRejected, validationIssues, mode="run", nodeStatus and onNodeSelect passed to FlowBuilder; codePanel passes readOnly, markers, onValidityChange, onMonacoReady and loader to an optional CodePanel (branch, parallel, sequence and worker-backed YAML examples). The app must import '@gntik-ai/flow/styles.css' once for the canvas styles. Optional nodeTypes, onConnectEdge, onConnect, isValidConnection, onConnectionRejected, validationIssues, mode, nodeStatus and onNodeSelect pass to FlowBuilder unchanged (see its branch, parallel and sequence examples). mode="run" hides Save, Publish and the saved notice, and preserves focus and node selection. Optional codePanel renders a companion CodePanel and passes all its extensions: readOnly, markers, onValidityChange, onMonacoReady and loader; run mode forces its readOnly to true. For example, WorkflowBuilderPage mode="run" nodeStatus={{step:"running"}} onNodeSelect={openDetails}; codePanel={{files,problems:[],loader:yamlLoader,markers}} uses consumer-owned same-origin YAML workers and inline schemas.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/templates` · export `WorkflowBuilderPage` · group Builders · status experimental
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/templates/src/workflow-builder/template.meta.ts
- Layout: CanvasLayout
- Blocks: flow-builder, code-panel
- Console shell: no
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=template&id=workflow-builder
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/templates`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add workflow-builder`

Usage:

```tsx

// Every prop is optional: unset ones fall back to the template fixtures.

  return <WorkflowBuilderPage />;
}
```

### Live event stream (`live-event-stream`)

Controlled subscription form inside FormSection, a visible StatusDot connection indicator, a quiet role=log stream with LogViewer windowing, search, follow-tail and copy, and a pinnable JSON inspector on InspectorLayout. No fetching or transport; no trace waterfall, token cost or timer.

## Props

LiveEventStreamPage accepts Partial<LiveEventStreamProps>; omitted props use generic fixtures.

| Prop | Type | Default / behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| title | string | Live event stream; PageHeader h1 |
| description | string | Subscribe to a source and inspect the events it emits. |
| form | ReactNode | Non-sensitive Source field inside FormSection; sensitive fields must use the kit PasswordInput |
| status | idle / connecting / live / error / stopped | idle; fully controlled |
| events | LiveEvent[] | Empty fixture; unique id, timestamp, type, optional summary and unknown payload; oldest first |
| maxEvents | number | 500; nonnegative integer; retains newest entries, evicts oldest; invalid values use 500 |
| eventTypes | string[] | created, updated, deleted; multiple ToggleGroup, initially all enabled; unlisted types remain visible |
| countAnnouncement | string | Omitted; optional count text throttled by the consumer, never inferred from events.length |
| onSubscribe | () => void | Subscribe callback in idle, stopped and error; disabled while connecting |
| onStop | () => void | Stop callback while live |
| onSelectEvent | (event: LiveEvent) => void | Mouse or keyboard selection callback |
| error | string | Generic subscription error; ErrorPanel shown when status=error, inside role=alert |
| validationMessage | string | Omitted; destructive InlineCallout |
| shell | Omit<ConsoleShellProps, 'children'> | ConsoleShell fixture defaults; explicit consumer navigation, workspace, user and topbar slots |

Status mapping: idle = neutral Not subscribed; connecting = info Connecting with pulse; live = success Live with pulse; error = destructive Error; stopped = warning Stopped. Subscribe is shown in idle/connecting/error/stopped and is disabled for connecting; live shows Stop. Idle has No events yet, live-empty has Listening for events, connecting replaces the log with decorative skeletons, and stopped keeps supplied buffered events visible.

## ARIA pattern

PageHeader h1 and labelled FormSection. One polite atomic live region announces connection status and explicit consumer-throttled count text only. LogViewer uses announceLines=false: role=log and aria-live=off; event additions are silent. Connecting uses an aria-busy section. Stream errors use ErrorPanel inside role=alert; validation uses InlineCallout. Inspect buttons have the name Inspect event <timestamp> and aria-pressed. InspectorLayout owns the complementary landmark on desktop, Drawer on small screens, docking, pinning and focus return. Pinning does not freeze the payload: subsequent selection updates it; eviction preserves the last inspected payload with the note This event is no longer in the buffer.

## Keyboard table

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Form fields, Subscribe/Stop, filters, search, Follow, row inspect/copy and panel controls |
| Enter / Space | Activate buttons; select an event; toggle Follow and pinning |
| Arrow keys | Navigate ToggleGroups and the JsonViewer tree |
| Escape | From unpinned panel or toggle, close and return focus to inspector toggle; pinned panel ignores Escape, Close panel closes it |

Follow pins the bottom, where the newest row is added. Scrolling up by more than one row turns Follow off and preserves the viewport offset; switching Follow on returns to the bottom.

## Themes and examples

Dark (default), light and high_contrast use only kit tokens. Connecting/live pulses stop under prefers-reduced-motion. State previews: live-event-stream--connecting, --live-empty, --live-with-events, --error and --stopped. Every state and the default template are covered by axe in all three themes.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/templates` · export `LiveEventStreamPage` · group Builders · status experimental
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/templates/src/live-event-stream/template.meta.ts
- ARIA pattern: PageHeader h1, labelled FormSection, one polite atomic connection live region, quiet role=log stream (aria-live=off), alert errors and complementary JSON inspector. Selected inspect buttons expose aria-pressed.
- Layout: InspectorLayout
- Blocks: app-sidebar, app-topbar, page-header, form-section, log-viewer, empty-states, skeletons, inline-callout, error-panel
- Console shell: yes (pass the product frame through the `shell` prop)
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=template&id=live-event-stream
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/templates`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add live-event-stream`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Navigate form, action, filters, search, Follow, row inspect/copy and panel controls. |
| Enter / Space | Activate buttons, select an event and toggle Follow or pinning. |
| Arrow keys | Navigate ToggleGroups and the JSON tree. |
| Escape | Close an unpinned inspector from panel or toggle and return focus to the toggle. Pinned panels ignore Escape. |

Usage:

```tsx
import { LiveEventStreamPage } from '@gntik-ai/templates';

// Every prop is optional: unset ones fall back to the template fixtures.
export default function Route() {
  return <LiveEventStreamPage shell={{ currentHref: '/', nav: undefined /* your NavGroup[] */ }} />;
}
```

### Create wizard (`create-wizard`)

Focus-mode create flow on WizardLayout. Without flowSteps, the existing details, source, configuration and editable review flow, CreateWizardProps, copy and defaults are unchanged. Page mode is the default; mode="overlay" keeps the parent list mounted without a route change. Overlay size defaults to fullscreen; size="dialog" uses a popup (fullscreen on mobile). Legacy closing preserves answers; confirming exit in flow mode resets answers and the current step.

## Caller-defined flow mode

Import CreateWizardPage (or CreateWizardFlow) and CreateWizardFlowProps<V> from @gntik-ai/templates. flowSteps selects the additive generic variant; legacy-only props (steps, copy, sources, regions, title, stepFeedback, onStepChange) cannot mix with it. V is the caller's object type. The kit owns current step, values and validation visibility. The display-only Stepper follows the supplied order and appends review. Zero caller steps renders review directly.

| Prop | Type / behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| flowSteps | readonly { id: string; label: string; readOnly?: boolean; render({ values, setValue, errors }): ReactNode; validate?(values): { fieldErrors?, blocking? } }[]; ids must be unique and stable |
| initialValues | V; used at mount and restored on confirmed exit |
| summary | (values: V) => readonly { stepId: string; label: string; value?: string or null }[] |
| labels | Required CreateWizardFlowLabels; no template-owned visible or accessible copy has a fallback |
| onFinish | (values: V, { signal: AbortSignal }) => void or Promise<unknown>; one signal per attempt |
| onExit | Called once after confirmed exit, after reset and abort; Stay calls nothing |
| onComplete | Uncontrolled only; (result: unknown) => void, once after success is committed and announced |
| submitState | Controlled when provided at mount: {status:'idle'}, {status:'submitting'}, {status:'success', result?:unknown}, or {status:'error', error?:unknown, message?:string} |
| resourceHref | (result: unknown) => string or undefined; only called with a non-null success result |
| errorMessage | (error: unknown) => string or undefined; empty text uses labels.errorFallback |
| confirmExit | Defaults to true; Exit, Escape and overlay Cancel open confirmation. false exits directly |
| mode, size, open, onOpenChange, description, returnFocusRef, closeOnInteractOutside | WizardLayout presentation props; closing itself is not confirmation or reset |

labels supplies title, exit, cancel, back, next, finish, pending, review (Stepper label), reviewTitle (heading), edit(stepLabel), emptyValue, success(result), errorFallback, openResource, exitTitle, exitDescription, exitConfirm, exitCancel, steps (Stepper name), stepsSummary, skipLink, stepStatusText (complete/current/upcoming/error), formatStepCount(position,total) and stepAnnouncement({position,total,label}). Positions are one-based. Step labels, validation messages, summary labels/values and rendered body content also belong to the caller's namespace. Every DescriptionListCard receives the owning step label as its explicit title, labels.edit(stepLabel), explicit items and an empty description. All steps get a card, even with no matching rows; empty values use labels.emptyValue.

## Validation and navigation

validate runs on every render, including caller re-renders (for example members.count quota changes). A non-empty blocking message disables Next immediately. It is visible as ordinary text and announced politely once per new value, including entry and one frame after overlay opening. Clearing blocking re-enables Next without a press. fieldErrors is Partial<Record<keyof V,string>>. Errors become visible after the first Next press on their step and remain live thereafter. With errors, Next does not advance and focuses the first aria-invalid="true" field. Render fields using Field invalid, FieldLabel, Input and FieldError to associate errors and controls. Blocking does not hide visible field errors. A readOnly step must render its fixed value as text, without editable controls; only its blocking result gates Next and its fieldErrors are ignored. Back, Next and review Edit preserve values. Edit returns to the owning step and focuses its heading. No direct Stepper jumps are available.

## Submit ownership and aborts

In uncontrolled mode, Finish shows labels.pending in both presentations. Resolve commits success, announces labels.success(result) politely, then calls onComplete(result) once. Reject keeps values and review, renders errorMessage(error) or labels.errorFallback, announces assertively and re-enables Finish. Identical repeated failures each announce; changing settled error text announces once, unchanged text does not. Visible success, error and blocking text is never a live region. All announcements use useAnnounce from the nearest LiveAnnouncer; the template provides one only when needed. Put LiveAnnouncer at page level when onComplete closes/unmounts the flow, so the message survives.

Controlled mode renders submitState only. Each enabled Finish press calls the existing onFinish once; its returned result never changes kit state and onComplete is never called. The caller must pass through submitting for every attempt, discard completions when signal.aborted, and reset submitState to idle in onExit before reopening. Switching between controlled and uncontrolled after mount is unsupported. AbortSignal is a cancellation contract, not a transport: callers must honor it. Confirmed exit and unmount abort the current attempt. Uncontrolled aborted settlements cannot update state, announce or complete, including an older attempt settling after reopening.

While submitting or after success, Back has backDisabled (aria-disabled but focusable), review cards have no Edit, and Finish is loading or disabled. Exit remains enabled. Pending Finish and locked Back retain focus. A focused control becoming disabled or removed sends focus on success to the resource link, or to the success heading (tabIndex=-1) if no result/href exists; in all other cases it goes to the current heading. Focus never moves to a live region. Page Back/Next preserve focus unless the pressed control becomes disabled. Overlay step changes focus the new heading and announce via LiveAnnouncer. Escape in a portalled Select or Menu stays local.

## Examples

examples/Invite.tsx is a generic single-recipient invite with a read-only workspace context, one email checked against /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/, a members.count quota, exactly Owner/Admin/Member roles, and an optional message with maxLength=500. Its copy is one English page namespace. examples/labels.ts lists every required label. UncontrolledPending, UncontrolledSuccess and UncontrolledError cover a never-settling attempt, a success resource link and a failure fallback. ControlledIdle, ControlledSubmitting, ControlledSuccess and ControlledError show each caller-owned state. Every example has a create-wizard--<kebab-name> preview entry; Invite uses create-wizard--invite. The three-theme browser axe loop visits each step, review, submit state and exit confirmation. examples/Overlay.tsx retains the original list-to-overlay project flow with step-local error and empty surfaces.

A controlled caller's onFinish can use this pattern (with its own transport, values and state): setSubmitState({status:'submitting'}); try { const result = await save(values, {signal}); if (!signal.aborted) setSubmitState({status:'success',result}); } catch (error) { if (!signal.aborted) setSubmitState({status:'error',error}); }. onExit resets to idle before reopening. Keep the page-level LiveAnnouncer mounted when closing.

All flow surfaces reuse kit components and existing tokens; no new CSS variables. Themes: dark, light and high_contrast.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/templates` · export `CreateWizardPage` · group Resources · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/templates/src/create-wizard/template.meta.ts
- ARIA pattern: Caller-defined steps and review with display-only progress; explicit labels; field-error associations; one LiveAnnouncer announcement mechanism; abortable submit lifecycle.
- Layout: WizardLayout
- Blocks: description-list-card, error-panel, empty-states
- Console shell: no
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=template&id=create-wizard
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/templates`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add create-wizard`

Keyboard:

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Move through Exit, fields, review Edit and footer controls; the Stepper is display-only. |
| Enter / Space on Next | Validate; focus the first invalid field, or advance. Blocking disables Next. |
| Enter / Space on Back | Return one step; disabled on the first page step and locked while submitting or after success. |
| Enter on Edit | Return to the owning step and focus its heading, preserving answers. |
| Escape / Exit | Open exit confirmation; Stay does nothing, Leave resets answers and aborts the attempt. Portalled popups handle their own Escape. |
| Finish | Call onFinish once when enabled; pending keeps focus, success hands focus to a resource link or the success heading if Finish becomes disabled. |

Usage:

```tsx
import { CreateWizardPage } from '@gntik-ai/templates';

// Every prop is optional: unset ones fall back to the template fixtures.
export default function Route() {
  return <CreateWizardPage />;
}
```

### Resource detail (`resource-detail`)

Resource detail with editable Overview, Activity and Settings tabs by default; optional readOnly (boolean, default false) uses only explicit header and detail props and one Overview tab, with optional history (readonly StatusEvent[], default undefined): omitted hides the history card, [] shows the named empty state, and events render exactly as supplied without invented actors. Read-only ignores activity, events, dangerActions, defaultTab, onSaveSettings and onDangerAction; explicit actions and onEditDetails are honored. The Resource sections tablist retains Tab, arrow, Home/End and Enter/Space keyboard navigation; history is a named group containing the Status history list or empty-state region. Uses token styling in dark (default), light and high_contrast. Examples: runtime-with-transition maps state and lastTransitionAt to one actor-free event, runtime-without-transition maps null to [], and realtime-configuration and postgres-table-detail omit history. Optional labels?: Partial<ResourceDetailLabels> overrides overview, activity, settings and sections (all strings). Unset keys use I18nProvider (en/es); no provider keeps English. Only the tabs and tablist are localized by this template; fixtures and other section text are unchanged. readOnly keeps only the localized overview tab. See the Catalog labels live preview. ConsoleShell retains sample frame defaults when shell is omitted or an object. shell={null} renders only Page and PageHeader, with breadcrumbs in the header; pass breadcrumbs or [] to avoid the editable sample trail. The host owns main and provides ChartLocaleProvider for custom chart locales. Optional tabs?: { value: string; label: string; content: ReactNode }[] replaces the built-in tabs in caller order, even with readOnly; [] hides the tab set. With custom tabs, defaultTab and onTabChange use string values; an omitted or unknown defaultTab selects the first tab. Without tabs they retain ResourceDetailTab values. Custom tabs use the same Base UI keyboard navigation and panel mounting. See the embedded-custom-tabs live preview for shell-less composition inside a host main.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/templates` · export `ResourceDetailPage` · group Resources · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/templates/src/resource-detail/template.meta.ts
- Layout: SidebarLayout + Page
- Blocks: app-sidebar, app-topbar, page-header, description-list-card, status-timeline, activity-feed, form-section, danger-zone
- Console shell: yes (pass the product frame through the `shell` prop)
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=template&id=resource-detail
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/templates`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add resource-detail`

Usage:

```tsx

  return <ResourceDetailPage shell={{ currentHref: '/', nav: undefined /* your NavGroup[] */ }} />;
}
```

### Profile settings (`settings-profile`)

Personal profile defaults to mode='editable': avatar header, name and email, locale and time zone, with a sticky save bar. Opt into mode='read-only' for an initials avatar without upload or Edit actions, identity and optional context description lists, and optional ordered roles badges. identity/context accept { id, label, value, mono } rows; value may be a link. contextFallback supplies missing-value text; emptyRolesMessage supplies the empty roles state. Omitted roles/context hide their sections. Read-only mode passes saveBar='none' through SettingsFrame and has no profile form controls, copy buttons or save actions; the responsive section navigation remains available.

### 404 Not found (`status-404`)

Full-page not-found state: code, message, a primary way home, Go back and a support link. The optional heading slot replaces the built-in title so PageHeader supplies the only h1; code stays above it and actions remain unchanged. In the PageHeader example set as="div", breadcrumbs={null}, meta={[]}, tabs={null}, actions={[]}, status="" and description={null}; use StatusLayout’s description once. PageHeader titleRef adds tabIndex=-1 for ref.current.focus() on route load without a Tab stop; leave slot links and actions empty to keep the primary action first in main.

- Package: `@gntik-ai/templates` · export `Status404Page` · group System · status beta
- Docs: https://github.com/gntik-ai/gntik-ui/blob/main/packages/templates/src/status-404/template.meta.ts
- Layout: StatusLayout
- Blocks: page-header
- Console shell: no
- Preview: /preview.html?kind=template&id=status-404
- Install: import from `@gntik-ai/templates`, or copy the source with `gntik-ui add status-404`

Usage:

```tsx
import { Status404Page } from '@gntik-ai/templates';

// Every prop is optional: unset ones fall back to the template fixtures.
export default function Route() {
  return <Status404Page />;
}
```
